title: OSNIP: Balancing the Privacy-Utility-Efficiency Trilemma in LLM Inference via Obfuscated Semantic Null Space
claim: A trusted party trains a key-conditioned encryptor that lets clients perturb embeddings into a null space, protecting privacy while keeping server inference unchanged.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right: server, third party, client, plus a sphere inset
description: A system diagram with three colored rounded regions. A green Server panel at top left holds an LLM-in-cloud box and a perturbed-embedding-to-clean-output stream. A blue Trusted Third Party panel at bottom left shows the training dataset (corpus and random keys), an MLP with hyperspherical projection, a multi-objective loss, and the resulting encryptor. A purple Client panel in the center holds the prompt, secret key, original embedding, encryptor and perturbed embedding z. Dashed gray arrows carry the query, response, gradient and the encryptor sent to the client. A crossed-out hacker icon, with KNN and vocabulary-matching attack icons, marks blocked attacks. On the right, a large sphere inset shows the original embedding h, a gray geometric obfuscation band, green semantic null-space rings, and a pink patch marking the obfuscated space reached with the user key.
caption: The OSNIP Architecture. Trusted Third Party trains an encryptor using corpora and randomized keys before deploying it client-side. Using their prompts and private keys, clients generate perturbed embeddings that resist privacy attacks by servers or interceptors, while still enabling standard server-side inference.
abstract: We propose Obfuscated Semantic Null space Injection for Privacy (OSNIP), a lightweight client-side encryption framework for privacy-preserving LLM inference. Generalizing the geometric intuition of linear kernels to the high-dimensional latent space of LLMs, we formally define the ``Obfuscated Semantic Null Space'', a high-dimensional regime that preserves semantic fidelity while enforcing near-orthogonality to the original embedding. By injecting perturbations that project the original embedding into this space, OSNIP ensures privacy without any post-processing. Furthermore, OSNIP employs a key-dependent stochastic mapping that synthesizes individualized perturbation trajectories unique to each user. Evaluations on 12 generative and classification benchmarks show that OSNIP achieves state-of-the-art performance, sharply reducing attack success rates while maintaining strong model utility under strict security constraints.
